reading: A loose small shape is erased from its place and redrawn inside the interior of the rectangular 6-outline, stretched to fill that interior (a full square fills it, an L becomes a full left column plus full bottom row).

slots.subject: the one object that is not the rectangular outline
slots.resize: subject's box stretched to the interior size, thin parts stay one cell wide along their edge

why: the frame interior holds the subject's shape stretched to the interior box; the subject's old cells are background; the outline is unchanged

reading: The input is scaled up by k = number of non-background colours; then colour-2 diagonal lines are drawn from each corner of the inner square outward until they hit the coloured border bands or the grid edge.
verb: scale up then draw corner diagonals

slots.factor: count of distinct non-background colours in the input
slots.subject: the inner filled square (not touching the right/bottom bands)
slots.lines: colour 2 diagonals from the four outer corners of the scaled square, through background only, stopping at non-background or grid edge

why: output = k-fold pixel upscale of input plus 2-diagonals leaving every corner of the scaled square and ending at the first non-background cell or edge

reading: Coloured cells sit on odd coordinates of a 10x10 grid; each cell at (r,c) becomes a 4x4 block of its colour at (2r-2, 2c-2) in a 20x20 output (equivalently: take the 5x5 grid of odd cells and scale it by 4).

slots.sample: cells at odd rows and odd columns (5x5 lattice)

why: every 4x4 block of the output is uniform and equals the input cell at (2i+1, 2j+1)

reading: A full-row/full-column cross of colour C splits the grid; the shape in the top-left quadrant is recoloured to C and reflected left-right and up-down, giving a 2x2 symmetric output of twice the quadrant size (separator dropped).
verb: recolour and reflect into four quadrants

slots.unit: top-left panel cut by the separator cross
slots.reflect: unit, its horizontal mirror to the right, vertical mirror below, and 180-degree copy diagonally

why: output is symmetric about both centre axes and its top-left quarter is the top-left panel with every fg cell set to the separator colour

reading: Swap the two colours (background 0 and the one foreground colour), then tile the inverted grid 2x2.
why: every one of the 4 output blocks equals the input with 0 and its foreground colour exchanged

reading: The 8-shape (in a 3x3 box, bottom-aligned when only 2 rows tall) is copied side by side once for every colour-4 cell in the input.

slots.unit: 3x3 box holding the 8 object (padded to 3x3 with an empty top row when the object is 2 rows tall)
slots.layout: copies placed left to right in one row

why: output is 3 rows by 3*n columns, n = number of 4-cells, each 3x3 block equals the 8 shape's box

reading: Vertical 8-segments have even lengths; one segment has half of its cells (top or bottom half) coloured 9. The 9 half is cleared back to 8 and moved to the segment two cells longer, on the same half (top/bottom).
verb: advance half-mark to next longer segment

slots.subject: the vertical segment containing 9 cells
slots.target: the vertical 8-segment whose length is the subject's length + 2
slots.mark: colour 9 on the same half (top or bottom) of the target, half its length

why: exactly one segment holds 9s in input and output; output's 9-segment is 2 longer than input's, with 9 on half of it at the same end; all else unchanged

reading: The 3x3 input is placed into a 9x9 output at each block whose position matches a cell of the input's least frequent colour; other blocks are 0.

new_rows.name: rare
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
minc(min(N)) :- ccount(C, N).
rare(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), minc(N).

why: block (i,j) of the output is the input iff input cell (i,j) has the colour with the fewest pixels, else all 0

reading: The coloured rows at the top are reflected to the bottom of the grid about its horizontal centre line.
why: output is the input plus its vertical reflection, symmetric about the horizontal midline

reading: The single odd-coloured cell grows into a filled rectangle of its colour spanning from it to the nearest grid corner.

new_rows.name: corner_box
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rsel(Y) :- cell(MY, MX, C), maxy(H), px(Y, X, K), D = H - MY, MY <= D, Y <= MY.
rsel(Y) :- cell(MY, MX, C), maxy(H), px(Y, X, K), D = H - MY, MY > D, Y >= MY.
csel(X) :- cell(MY, MX, C), maxx(W), px(Y, X, K), D = W - MX, MX <= D, X <= MX.
csel(X) :- cell(MY, MX, C), maxx(W), px(Y, X, K), D = W - MX, MX > D, X >= MX.
corner_box(Y, X) :- rsel(Y), csel(X), px(Y, X, K).

why: every cell in the box between the marker and its nearest grid corner takes the marker's colour; nothing else changes
